result:
Staging this as a new project: nothing works end to end yet (the package is the greeting `main()` and two smoke tests), and there's no spec. I'm using your research brief (`specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`) as your words and the three research files as background. Below are the outcomes, deliberately unranked. Before I write any roadmap text, I need you to rank them.

## Outcomes

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision series at each of the four stages (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back), SA and NSA, for total nonfarm and supersectors, from real-time vintages | Data volume is small (MB-scale: about 11 series × about 500 months × a handful of vintages). The real cost is vintage depth and access. ALFRED and BLS API rate limits are published. How far back supersector and NSA vintages go is unknown until probed. |
| O2 | A descriptive history of revision magnitude by stage: dispersion over time, with the 2003 break and 2020–22 marked | Negligible once O1 exists |
| O3 | SA one- and two-month revisions split into an NSA-sample component and a seasonal-factor component | Measured by its core stage. It depends on joint NSA/SA vintage depth from O1. |
| O4 | The effect of collection interval (days from the 12th to release, and closing rates) on one-month revision scale | Calendar days are cheap to compute. Closing-rate history has to be hand-collected from release tables, which needs probing to cost. |
| O5 | Annual covariate series: real BLS appropriations, FTE, CES sample size, shutdowns and CRs | Mostly your or my time. About 40 annual budget justifications plus FedScope. Roughly 1–2 days of extraction, based on document count. |
| O6 | Honestly shrunk estimates of funding, staffing and sample effects on revision scale, with the identification limits stated | Measured by its core stage |
| O7 | A multi-vintage state-space model: latent true path, news/noise by stage, benchmark as an irregular high-precision observation with wedge-back, Student-t errors with SV and covariates in log-scale, supersector pooling, and PPC/LOO/pseudo-real-time validation | NUTS compute can't be estimated without a real fit, so its core stage measures it |

## Tracks

- **A: Vintage data and description (O1, O2). Known progression,** if you can name its stages. Every other track consumes O1, so A's core stage goes first whatever the ranking.
- **B: Seasonal vs sample (O3). Research.** Its answer stands without any other track's.
- **C: Collection interval (O4). Research.** I split it from D because within-year calendar variation identifies it, while D rests on slow, collinear annual series. Either answer stands alone.
- **D: Institutional capacity (O5, O6). Research.**
- **E: Joint state-space model (O7). Research.** It could absorb B through D as components. I kept it separate so those questions don't wait on its machinery.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv (from `.python-version` and `uv.lock`).
- NumPyro, Dynamax, Blackjax, ArviZ and Polars (from the brief). JAX support on 3.14 needs checking before E's core stage.
- Party of the appropriators is descriptive only, not a causal slope (from the brief).

**Proposed name:** `ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`.

**One optional probe:** I could fetch the ALFRED vintage list for PAYEMS and one supersector to firm up O1's cost. I'd only run it if you say yes.

**What I need from you:** rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds (especially A's) and the name.
